title: Compare repair stiffness under unknown tensile load, then preserve nutrient supply and maturation costs
status_authority: Actual version-bound scoped internal review governs acceptance. Source reports, mathematical verification and physical acquisition remain separate.
reported_status: accepted_internally_verified for exact conditional elastic, ODE and observation arguments; reported growth populations, primary component experiments and integrated biological repair remain separate evidence gaps.
scientific_scope_status: Two linear elastic branches with top/bottom stiffnesses a,b and c,d, positive shared extension Delta and midpoint probe k>=0 give g=Delta*(c*b-a*d)/[(a+b)*(c+d)+k*(a+b+c+d)]; sign(g) compares d with c*b/a independently of positive load magnitude. Zero drive gives no signal. Multiple finite probes require joint calibration. In a separate instantaneous response model, a cubically closing nutrient slit gives e_dot=-A*e^3 and asymptotic exact completion; a positive nutrient threshold can stop it earlier. Delayed precursor stock can keep adding stiffness after feed stops. Reference drift, nonlinear elasticity and aliased incomplete states prevent this scalar response from universally certifying strength or choosing the missing construction action.
